issues.failure_explanation: With the transforms exactly as displayed (unnormalized forward DFT in step 2, unnormalized inverse DFT in step 4), the spread data satisfy $\hat a_{\bk}=m^3\sum_{\br}c_{\bk+m\br}(\tilde\varphi\text{-data})\approx \frac{m^3}{V}\hat\varphi(\bk)\hat\rho(\bk)$, not $\hat\rho(\bk)\hat\varphi(\bk)$ as asserted (a factor $m^3/V=1/h^3$ is dropped), and the interpolation step contributes another factor $m^3c_{\bk}$. Composing the five steps therefore returns $\frac{m^6}{V^2}\phi_i^{\text{far}}$ instead of $\phi_i^{\text{far}}$: with the displayed transforms the correct diagonal factor is $\frac{V}{m^6}\frac{\hat M(\bk)}{\hat\varphi(\bk)^2}$ (equivalently, the deconvolution must use the grid DFT of the sampled window, or $h^3$ factors must appear in spreading/interpolation). The same convention error appears in the aliasing identity (eq:alias): for the displayed (unnormalized) DFT of grid samples one has $\hat f_{\bk}=m^3\sum_{\br}c_{\bk+m\br}(f)$, so the stated identity is missing the factor $m^3$. The matrix form (eq:matform) inherits the inconsistency.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Adopt and state one consistent normalization convention: e.g., deconvolve by the window's grid DFT $\sum_{\bl}\tilde\varphi(h\bl)e^{2\pi i\bk\cdot\bl/m}$, or include $h^3$ in the spreading and interpolation steps, or replace $1/V$ in (eq:diag_scale) by $V/m^6$; correct (eq:alias) with the factor $m^3$.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm 2 as literally specified does not deliver its stated output contract: the returned far field is off by the factor $m^6/V^2=(m/L)^6$; the standalone identity (eq:alias) is off by $m^3$; and the deconvolution choice analyzed in Proposition prop:interpol_est does not match the algorithm as written. Several inequivalent-looking repairs exist (grid-DFT deconvolution, $h^3$ factors, rescaled diagonal), so this is not a pure typo. The error analysis propositions are internally self-consistent and the reported numerics necessarily used a consistent normalization, so no substantive claim about the method changes.
issues.title: FFT/window normalization inconsistency in the fast Ewald algorithm
issues.why_classification: The defect is purely a normalization-convention inconsistency: the repair is a short, local, routine convention fix (with several standard equivalent choices), and every substantive claim, rate, and guarantee survives unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The display assigns to one function two properties that cannot hold simultaneously: per-coordinate bandlimit $c_w/\alpha$ (true only of the bandlimited extension of $\psi_0^{c_w}$ to $\R$, whose per-coordinate transform is $\frac{2\pi}{c_w\lambda_0}\psi_0^{c_w}(\alpha\omega_i/c_w)/\psi_0^{c_w}(0)$, not $\lambda_0\psi_0^{c_w}(\alpha\omega_i/c_w)/\psi_0^{c_w}(0)$ as displayed) and the displayed transform formula, which by Lemma lem:PSWFrelation is the finite-interval transform, i.e., the transform of the compactly supported truncated window $\varphi_t^{c_w}$ (which is entire, hence not bandlimited). The paper's actual usage (deconvolution on grid modes, Table tab:reference_windows, the sentence after (eq:truncwindow)) is that of the truncated window, for which the formula is correct on the band cube; the bandlimit clause is then false. Moreover, outside-band values are in fact required and used — cubic-grid corner modes have $|\bomega|$ up to $\sqrt3\,\omega_{\max}=\sqrt3\,c_s/r_c>c_s/r_c$, the reference computation is explicitly 'evaluated at all available wavenumbers (also outside the bandlimit)', and prop:interpol_est evaluates $\psi_0^{c_w}$ at arguments in $[1,3]$ — contradicting the claims (in sec:PSWF_mollifier and in the Table tab:mollifiers caption) that the outside-band region is 'never used in practice'. Finally, the extension of $\psi_0^c$ beyond $[-1,1]$ that all these outside-band evaluations presuppose is never defined, and Lemma lem:PSWFrelation (the identity licensing them) is stated only for $\omega\in[-c,c]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the bandlimited extension of $\psi_0^c$ to $\R$ (via the eigenvalue integral for all $s\in\R$), extend Lemma lem:PSWFrelation to all $\omega$, attribute the displayed FT formula to the truncated window (dropping the bandlimit clause) or to the extension (with the corrected per-coordinate constant $2\pi/(c_w\lambda_0)$), and correct the two 'never used' remarks.
issues.overall_effect: The PSWF window's Fourier characterization is internally inconsistent (no function satisfies both clauses of (eq:PSWFwindow_ft)); two practical claims about outside-band values never being used are false; and prop:interpol_est as written evaluates the PSWF on $[1,3]$ where the paper has not defined it. issues.title: PSWF window Fourier transform conflates truncated window with bandlimited extension; outside-band values used but undefined
issues.why_classification: The repairs are short, local, and forced (a standard extension definition plus corrected statements); every formula actually used downstream is already correct under this repair, so no substantive claim, rate, or guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem:cubecover applies only to nonincreasing radial functions, but no hypothesis of lemma:dirsumerr_L2 ensures that $|\hat M(\bomega)|^2=16\pi^2|\hat\gamma_\sigma(|\bomega|)|^2/|\bomega|^4$ is nonincreasing: the paper's mollifier definition requires only evenness, non-negativity, unit mass, and a pointwise tail bound. For the PSWF mollifier — the case the bound is used for in prop:PSWF_split_errors — the property is false: $\gamma_{r_c}^{c_s}$ jumps to zero at $\pm r_c$ (since $\psi_0^{c_s}(1)>0$), so its Fourier transform has a slowly decaying oscillatory tail beyond the band (the paper itself refers to 'slowly decaying sinc-type oscillations in the PSWF spectrum'), and the sum $\sum_{|\bk|>\Kmax}$ with $\omega_{\max}=c_s/r_c$ runs precisely over that non-monotone beyond-band region. The invoked estimate is therefore used outside its hypotheses in the paper's central case.

issues.why_classification: Preserving the exponential rate requires a new, contained tail-envelope lemma for the PSWF extension (more than a routine local fix), but the bound's form and all rates survive with modified constants, and the empirically validated models are unaffected — a recognizably comparable result remains.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims $C_*\approx1$, but by the paper's own definition $C_* = 1+(\omega_{\max}/\omega_*)^2\,\mu_0/(1-\mu_0)$ with $\mu_0=c_s\lambda_0^2/(2\pi)$, and Fuchs' asymptotics ((eq:fuchs), cited in rem:eig_errors) give $1-\mu_0\sim4\sqrt{\pi c_s}\,e^{-2c_s}$; hence $C_*$ grows like $e^{2c_s}/(4\sqrt{\pi c_s})$ (e.g., $\sim4\times10^8$ at $c_s\approx11.5$) — false by many orders of magnitude, for any $\omega_*/\omega_{\max}\approx1$. The bloat originates in the proof step $\int_{\omega_*}^{\omega_{\max}}|\hat\gamma|^2\le\int_0^{\omega_{\max}}|\hat\gamma|^2$, which replaces the exponentially small energy of the narrow sliver $[\omega_*,\omega_{\max}]$ near the band edge by the full $\mathcal O(1)$ in-band energy. Consequently the bound actually proved in prop:PSWF_split_errors is $C_*(2\pi/\lambda_0^2-c_s)=(2\pi/\lambda_0^2-c_s)+c_s(\omega_{\max}/\omega_*)^2\sim c_s$, i.e., the squared-error bound decays only algebraically ($\sim c_s^{-3/2}$, RMS $\sim c_s^{-3/4}$), not exponentially; at practical tolerances the proven bound is orders of magnitude above the model. The derivation of the exponential closed-form model (eq:PSWF_model) from the proposition is therefore invalid as written, and the Section 5 claim of 'establishing exponential error decay and providing sharp bounds' is unsupported for the split error.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the $C_*\approx1$ claim and sharpen the in-band estimate in prop:PSWF_split_errors: using monotonicity of $|\hat\gamma_{r_c}^{c_s}|$ on the band, bound $\int_{\omega_*}^{\omega_{\max}}|\hat\gamma|^2\omega^{-2}d\omega\le |\hat\gamma(\omega_*)|^2/\omega_*$, which is exponentially small since $r_c\omega_*/c_s=1-\sqrt3/m$; restate the proposition with the resulting $\mathcal O(1)$ prefactor replacing $C_*$.
issues.overall_effect: The closed-form split-error model (eq:PSWF_model) loses its claimed rigorous derivation; the rigorous split bound of prop:PSWF_split_errors is algebraic and nearly vacuous at practical tolerances rather than exponential and sharp as advertised in the abstract and Section 5. The model itself, the fitted constants, the parameter-selection procedure, and all numerics remain valid (they are empirically confirmed).
issues.title: False claim that the prefactor $C_*$ is asymptotically negligible undermines the rigorous split-error bound
issues.why_classification: The false prefactor claim breaks the link between the rigorous bound and the exponential model — a real loss of the advertised 'rigorous, sharp, exponential' split theory — but a contained nontrivial repair (sharpening one proof step via on-band monotonicity) restores a comparable exponential bound, and all practical outputs survive on numerical validation; no global re-architecture or major loss.

issues.failure_explanation: The premise that $\psi_0^c$ is nonincreasing on $[0,\infty)$ is false: the extension of $\psi_0^c$ beyond $[-1,1]$ has an oscillatory, slowly decaying tail — equivalently, since $\hat\psi_0^c(\omega)=\lambda_0\psi_0^c(\omega/c)$, the 'slowly decaying sinc-type oscillations in the PSWF spectrum' that the paper itself displays and discusses. Both (eq:ratio-le-1) (used at arguments up to $\sqrt3>1$) and (eq:psi-at-least-edge) (which requires $|\psi_0^{c_w}(x)|\le\psi_0^{c_w}(1)$ for $x\in[1,3]$) rest on this false monotonicity claim, and they feed the reduction of the aliasing sum to (eq:axis-bound) and hence the closed-form model (eq:window_err_model). issues.failure_explanation: The argument of $W$ is a small negative number in $(-1/e,0)$, where two real branches exist. The default principal branch $W_0$ takes values in $(-1,0)$, producing $c_w=-\tfrac12W_0(\cdot)\in(0,\tfrac12)$ — e.g., $c_w\sim10^{-7}$ at typical parameters — whereas the intended solution of $c_w^{1/2}e^{-c_w}=B_wc_s^{-1/2}e^{-c_s}$ is the large root $c_w>c_s\gg1$ (consistent with the paper's use of $c_s<c_w$), which requires the $W_{-1}$ branch. As written, step 2 (and (eq:cwW)) returns the wrong root, leading to $\alpha\approx0$ and a meaningless window support $P$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify the $W_{-1}$ branch in (eq:cwW) and in step 2 of Algorithm alg:parameter.
issues.overall_effect: The parameter-selection procedure as literally specified computes a nonsensical window bandlimit, so its stated guarantee (parameters achieving the prescribed tolerance) fails; all other steps are unaffected.
issues.title: Lambert $W$ branch unspecified: principal branch yields the wrong root for $c_w$
issues.why_classification: The correction is a single forced branch specification that any competent reader/implementer must make; no inference, model, or guarantee changes once the branch is fixed.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated bound is false. Counterexample: $K=1>\sqrt3/2$ and $f=\mathbb 1_{[0,\sqrt2]}$ (nonincreasing, non-negative). The left side is $\#\{\bk\in\Z^3:1<|\bk|\le\sqrt2\}=\#\{|\bk|=\sqrt2\}=12$, while the right side is $\tfrac{4\pi}{3}\big((\sqrt2)^3-(1-\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2})^3\big)\approx 11.84$. The proof sketch is correspondingly invalid: monotonicity and $||\bx|-|\bk||\le\sqrt3/2$ give only $f(|\bk|)\le f(|\bx|-\sqrt3/2)$ on $Q_{\bk}$, whose radial change of variables produces an extra Jacobian factor $(1+\tfrac{\sqrt3/2}{|\by|+\sqrt3/2})^2$ and a lower integration limit $K-\sqrt3$ — both are dropped in the stated lemma. Standard corrected versions exist with modified constants.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace lem:cubecover by a correct covering bound, e.g. $\sum_{|\bk|>K}f(|\bk|)\le\int_{|\bx|>K-\sqrt3/2}f(|\bx|-\sqrt3/2)\,d\bx$ (or the equivalent version with lower limit $K-\sqrt3$ and the radial Jacobian factor), and propagate the modified constants through lemma:dirsumerr_L2 and prop:PSWF_split_errors.
issues.overall_effect: The lattice-to-continuum step in lemma:dirsumerr_L2 rests on a false lemma, so the constant 8 there (and the constants of prop:PSWF_split_errors that follow from it) are not justified; the shape, exponential rate, and practical content of the truncation bounds survive any standard corrected covering estimate.
issues.title: Lattice covering lemma is false as stated
issues.why_classification: The lemma is false with an explicit counterexample and its proof's key inference is invalid, so a corrected covering statement and proof are required and the constants in two downstream results must be reworked — more than a routine local fix — but the replacement is standard and contained, and every substantive claim and rate survives.
